## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Dhātupūjakattheraapadāna* is a verse text included in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddakanikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the biographical past deed (*apadāna*) of an elder (*thera*) associated with worship or making an offering to relics (*dhātu*). Translations of the text are cataloged on SuttaCentral in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No external parallels from Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are listed on SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive formulaic overlap within Pali literature, showing 84 matching passages across 37 texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest internal textual alignment is with the *Aparauttarattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 559), which shares an extended block of verses (§0.3–5.3) at a high degree of similarity [DharmaNexus]. Passages from the text (§1.1–2.3) are likewise mirrored in the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), while standard recurring verse segments (such as §2.2–7.1 and §3.1–7.1) are shared with numerous other offering-themed poems in the *Therāpadāna*, including the *Gandhapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 462), *Daṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 528), and *Paṁsukūlapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 494) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
